[element-std-id]
=== `<std-id>` Standard ID

One identifier (such as a DOI, URN, standard designator, or standards organization’s internal document ID) for a standard, using the <<attribute-std-relationship-type,`@std-relationship-type`>> attribute to name the type of identifier (such as dated or undated designations).

#### Usage/Remarks
Several <<element-std-id,`<std-id>`>> identifiers may be grouped into a container element <<element-std-id-group,`<std-id-group>`>> to indicate that they are alternative identifiers for the same standard. For example, such a group could contain: one <<element-std-id,`<std-id>`>> containing a DOI, a second <<element-std-id,`<std-id>`>> containing a URN, and a third containing a standards-producing organization’s internal-processing identifier. Thus each <<element-std-id,`<std-id>`>> (with its attributes) can be used inside the <<element-std-id-group,`<std-id-group>`>> element to support the coupling of identifiers, such as the designator and the URN, and to describe this relationship.

#### Tagged Sample

##### <<attribute-std-relationship-type,`@std-relationship-type`>> differentiates dated DOIs
[source,xml]
....
...
<std
 ><std-ref>ISO 9001:2015</std-ref>
 <std-id-group>
  <std-id 
    std-id-type="dated" 
    std-id-link-type="doi" 
    originator="ISO">10.9999/ISO-9001:2015</std-id>
  <std-id 
    std-id-type="dated" 
    std-id-link-type="doi"
    std-relationship-type="adopted-from" 
    originator="EN">10.9998/EN-ISO-9001:2015</std-id>
  <std-id 
    std-id-type="dated" 
    std-id-link-type="doi"
    std-relationship-type="adopted-from"
    originator="BSI" >10.9998/BS-EN-ISO-9001:2015</std-id>
 </std-id-group></std>
...
....
